detail.longDescription: "The next chapter of tech comm will be this: designing docs for agents. This is how we survive the AI transformation. If I can do 5 days of normal documentation work in 1 day due to the agent skills (combined with powerful models and tools), then the existing role of tech comm will need to expand in other ways. I thought that maybe engineering would accelerate in parallel and push out 5X as much code to document, but that’s not happening. Tech writing seems to be able to scale much faster than engineering code (which requires testing, validation, multi-stage review, etc.). I mean, there’s a whole software development lifecycle for code, but you can write and publish docs for a new feature in an hour. If we continue just performing our same role but more efficiently, there’s only one end for the tech writer: he or she becomes more and more solitary, expanding further across product areas. You might support 10 teams now, and in the future, it’ll be 15, and then 20, and before you know it, tech writers will cover vast swaths of documentation. Tech writers will be isolated lone wolves, interfacing virtually to support releases from teams they’ve never even met. Much of their work will involve reviewing and accepting the docs that engineering teams write. That’s a sad end to the tech writer story. I propose a shift in direction. From my vantage point, it’s the only logical shift to the profession. We are no longer writing just for humans. We’re now writing for agents. We need to become experts in agent behavior, in understanding how agents find, discover, retrieve, and consume information, from docs to product skills to other sources." https:// idratherbewriting.com/blog/pat h-to-reinventing-tech-comm-career # TechnicalWriting # TechnicalCommunications # AI # GenerativeAI # LLMs # AIAgents # SoftwareDocumentation # Automation # Productivity
